summary: Crawford County towersite bought 1946-47 south of Steelville; the 85 ft steel tower still stands on the property and is occasionally used in high fire danger.

facts.design: Four-legged steel structure with an 8-foot square house on top

access.note: The 80-acre towersite is open to hunting and other uses, and a service road gives some access. No source says the public may climb the tower.

visit.trail_note: From Steelville, take Route AA south 5 miles, then east on Tower Road.

events.note: 80 acres acquired for a towersite in 1946-1947; the 2019 plan gives 1947 as the initial acquisition year.

A June 28, 1947 newspaper item calls it one of the new towers, an 85-foot steel tower. The 2019 plan says it was constructed in the early 1950s, so the build year conflicts with 1947 and is unresolved; the story reports only the 1947 item.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record and the 1947-1956 sources name the Missouri Conservation Commission. The current MDC area page and the 2019 plan name the Missouri Department of Conservation, which is the current manager and is used in facts.

notes_for_editor: Built year is unresolved: a June 28, 1947 newspaper line calls the tower new, but the 2019 plan says it was constructed in the early 1950s. The story gives only the 1947 item.A Missouri Conservation History Facebook post (title only, body unreadable here) gives 1948; unverified, so not used. Climbing status is not stated in any source. Record height 25.9 m matches the 85 ft figure. Record agency is the 1947 name.
